lines: hook
Rent in from forty units. A drain call at the fourplex. A turnover paint job at Unit 6.
hook
Then the first of the month: an owner statement for every owner. Built by hand.
hook
And when your fee income blends in with owner rent, it's hard to see what your own business actually earns.
hook
So here's the question. Which units are actually worth [managing?]
hook
A lease that expires without a renewal conversation turns into an unplanned vacancy.
hook
If you run a property management company, the next few minutes are for you.

lines.text: If you run a property management company — [this is for you.]

lines: pain
Here's how the money side of property management usually works.
pain
Rent lives in one system. Work orders in another. Vendor invoices in your inbox.
pain
An empty unit costs lost rent every day, and owners will ask about it.
pain
Repairs get coordinated and paid. The total cost per unit rarely gets added up.
pain
Some properties take more maintenance and owner attention than their fees justify.
pain
Late rent, and balances owed, while vendors still need paying.
pain
Your accountant asks for everything. And nothing's in one place.
pain
Busy every month, and still not sure what the business actually kept.
turn
That's not a work-ethic problem. It's a visibility problem.
turn
You already have the data: rent rolls, leases, work orders, owner statements.
turn
You just don't have one place that turns it into decisions.

That's why we built the Property Management Business Intelligence System™.

reveal

reveal

who

who

who

Properties, tenants, leases, vacancy, maintenance, owners, rent, expenses, P&L, unit profitability, forecasts and taxes.

money

money

risk

risk
